answer: A farm that owns the submitting key cannot also own the verifiers, because each one must be independent on the signal graph and each exposes its bond to the cedar slash if it rubber-stamps. A verdict only settles when 2 independent verifiers reach the same tier, and the payout is withheld until they do. Since disagreement costs everyone the epoch, the vault audit records every split and the operator cannot buy agreement cheaply. That is 36 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
